THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SHIVASHANKAR AMARANNAVAR  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:13133  MFA No. 103129 of 2014
ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the order of the Tribunal to pay and recover passed in MVC No.955/2012 dated 10.09.2014 by the Court of Fast Track and Additional MACT, Dharwad.

entities.text: Court of Fast Track and Additional MACT, Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Respondent No.1 who was injured in a road traffic accident made a claim petition seeking compensation.

The Tribunal after recording evidence has awarded compensation of Rs.1,61,373/-
with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The Tribunal has directed the insurance company to pay compensation and to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle i.e. respondent No.2 herein.
The said order of the Tribunal is challenged in this appeal.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent No.1.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:13133 4.

Learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess driving licence and it has been established and it amounts to fundamental breach and the order of the Tribunal to pay and recover is not correct.
He further contends that the Tribunal awarding interest @ 8% per annum on the compensation is on the higher side.

5. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 contends that even though there is breach of any condition of policy or fundamental breach, as the insurer had undertaken to pay the 3 r d party risk,
the insurer is liable to pay the compensation and it has to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

On that point, he placed reliance on the decision of Full Bench of this Court rendered in New India Assurance Company Limited, Bijapur v. Yal lavva w/o Yamanappa Dharanakeri and another 1 2020 (2) AKR 484 NC: 2024:KHC-D:13133 6.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited, Bijapur v. Yal lavva w/o Yamanappa Dharanakeri and another 1 2020 (2) AKR 484 NC: 2024:KHC-D:13133 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel, the Court has perused the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

The Divisional Manager vs Channappa S/O Sidlingappa Dharwad on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160248668/
2 7.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Channappa S/O Sidlingappa Dharwad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal considering the evidence on record, has held that the rider of the motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the offending vehicle and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The Tribunal held respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle liable to pay the compensation and directed the insurance company to pay the compensation and recover it from respondent No.1.
The Tribunal has relied on the decision in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Smt. J.C. Ramadevi and others 2.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Smt. J.C. Ramadevi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Yallavva's case (supra) Full Bench of this Court has considered the said aspect in detail and has held that the insurer has undertaken to pay the 3 r d party risk and therefore, liable to pay the compensation to 3 r d party and recover the same 2014 KAR.MAC 119 (KAR) NC: 2024:KHC-D:13133 from insured even though there was a breach of any condition of the policy or fundamental breach.
Considering the said aspect, the judgment of the Tribunal, ordering to pay and recover cannot be found fault with.
8. The Tribunal has awarded interest on the compensation @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 8% per annum is on the higher side.

Interest as per the decisions of this Court and Apex Court has to be awarded at 6%
per annum.
9. In view of the above, the following ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.

The judgment and award dated 10.09.2014 passed by the Court of Fast Track and Additional MACT, Dharwad, in MVC No.955/2012 is modified only to the extent of reducing the rate of interest on the compensation NC:
2024:KHC-D:13133 from 8% per annum to 6% per annum.

entities.text: Court of Fast Track and Additional MACT, Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The other findings of the Tribunal remains unaltered.
The amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal concerned.
